topic: Operating model is the hidden AI lever
angle: AI value is an operating-model decision, not a model-performance decision.
sourceTitle: The key to AI value is hiding in plain sight: Your operating model
linkedinPost:
Most AI programs don’t stall on technology. They stall on the operating model.

A new McKinsey piece argues there isn’t one “best” AI org design—there are clear choices to make and then execute well. That maps to what I see as a Forward Deployed Engineer: the companies that get value don’t copy a chart; they pick a model and commit.

Three patterns separate the winners I’ve worked with:

- Ownership: a single throat to choke for each use case, from model to metrics.
- Cadence: a two-week ship rhythm with real business users, not quarterly demos.
- Interfaces: productized services (APIs, playbooks, guardrails) that any team can consume without a priesthood.

The tech is often “good enough.” The gaps are handoffs, incentives, and decision rights. When an LLM workflow dies in the last mile, it’s rarely because of accuracy—it’s because nobody owned the rollout, support, and change management.

My take: Decide if you’re hub-and-spoke, embedded, or platform-led—then lock in ownership, funding, and an operating rhythm for 12 months. Consistency beats brilliance in AI transformation.

Which operating-model choice tripped you up: ownership, cadence, or interfaces?
